subject: Operations
title: Shewhart and Control Charts
description: A short lesson to help you apply Shewhart and Control Charts.

hook.text: In 1924, Walter Shewhart drew two lines on a chart—upper and lower control limits. Modern quality was born.

buildup.text: Shewhart realized that variation is natural but some variation signals a real problem. The chart tells them apart.

discovery.text: Common cause variation is random and expected. Special cause variation means something changed—investigate it.

twist.text: Reacting to common cause variation—tampering—actually makes output worse. Know when to act and when to wait.

climax.text: Shewhart's PDCA cycle—plan, do, check, act—became the heartbeat of continuous improvement worldwide.

punchline.text: Two lines on a chart changed manufacturing forever.

quiz.question: What did Shewhart's control chart help distinguish?
